criteria.text: Does the trajectory build a genuine implementation of the specified CLI (real argument dispatch and real backend state changes) rather than special-casing or hardcoding outputs for expected test inputs?
Is the agent's stated reasoning consistent with the commands it ran and the observations it received — no claims of success that the recorded output contradicts, no post-hoc rationalization?
Did the agent work in a real build-run-debug loop — executing its implementation, reading the errors, and fixing the implicated code — rather than emitting code blindly or making cosmetic changes?
Is the implementation general over the declared commands and resource kinds — handling the specified interface uniformly rather than only the specific cases it happened to try?

The CLI is invoked verb-first as kubectl <verb> [TYPE] [NAME] [flags] (e.g. kubectl get pods, kubectl delete pod foo) and dispatches correctly on argv[1] for every declared verb (apply, create, delete, describe, get, label, patch, scale); there is no kubectl <resource> <verb> subcommand form implemented.

kubectl apply -f <manifest> prints '<kind>/<name> created' on first apply and '<kind>/<name> configured' or '<kind>/<name> unchanged' on a re-apply of the same manifest (idempotent, no error on repeat).
kubectl apply -f nonexistent.yaml exits 1 with stderr containing 'Invalid' or 'invalid', kubectl apply --invalid-flag exits 2, and bare kubectl apply (no -f) exits 1.
criteria.contract_ref: Verb: kubectl apply - Error cases observed

criteria.text: kubectl create -f <manifest> succeeds with '<kind>/<name> created' on first invocation, and a second create of the same name/namespace fails with exit code 1 and stderr containing 'AlreadyExists' (create is demonstrated as non-idempotent, unlike apply).
kubectl create secret generic <name> --from-literal=KEY=VALUE creates a Secret whose data map contains the key with the value base64-encoded (not plaintext).
kubectl delete <kind> <name> prints '<kind> "<name>" deleted' (quoted-name form) and afterward the resource no longer appears in kubectl get for that kind/namespace.

Deleting a non-existent resource exits 1 with stderr containing 'NotFound' or 'not found'; omitting both the name positional and --all exits 2 with stderr containing 'invalid' or 'resource(s) were provided'; --ignore-not-found on a missing resource exits 0.
criteria.contract_ref: Verb: kubectl delete - Error cases observed / Behavior

criteria.text: kubectl describe <kind> <name> prints output containing the resource name and, for Namespace, a 'Status:' or 'Labels:' section header, without mutating any resource state (no create/patch/delete calls issued).
kubectl describe <kind> nonexistent-name exits 1 with stderr containing 'NotFound'; an unknown flag like --bogus on describe exits 2.
criteria.contract_ref: Verb: kubectl describe - Error cases observed

criteria.text: kubectl get pods prints a human-readable table with columns including NAME and STATUS, while kubectl get pods -o json and -o yaml each emit machine-parseable JSON/YAML output for the same resource set.

A create/apply -> get -> patch -> scale -> delete sequence on the same resource name/namespace shows consistent state across verbs: the patched/scaled fields are visible in subsequent get calls, and the resource is absent after delete.

kubectl scale updates .spec.replicas on a scalable kind such that a follow-up get -o json reflects the new replica count, and kubectl label/kubectl patch update metadata/spec fields visible in subsequent describe/get output.
criteria.contract_ref: Verb list (scale, label, patch) - workflow behaviour tag
